c-surface-inventory.description: The Rust crate intentionally has no libxmlsec1 C ABI yet; every public C surface item remains visible rather than being implied by marketing copy.

legacy-policy-tests.description: Legacy SHA-1 signature paths are available only through explicit compatibility policy opt-ins.

native-algorithm-tests.description: The claimed URI set is cross-checked against the native algorithm parsers and the repository's unit and interop suites.

native-cli-tests.description: Process tests cover native command parsing, exit statuses, sign/verify and encrypt/decrypt paths; the unmodified upstream DSig, Enc, and Keys runners exercise the same binary and capability registry.

phaos-xmldsig-tests.description: The exhaustive Phaos integration suite executes every signature document through the public verification API and asserts exact valid, invalid, or unsupported outcomes without skips.

planned-surface.description: Unimplemented backend APIs, CLI, registry, format, URI, and donor-suite entries remain machine-readable planned work.

provider-contract.description: Only backend transform classes backed by native provider operations are provider-limited; every other backend-specific C entry point remains planned.

sha1-verification-tests.description: SHA-1 interoperability verification executes through the public pipeline; secure signing defaults reject SHA-1 while an explicit compatibility policy enables builder construction and signing.

unsupported-legacy-surface.description: Deprecated C compatibility aliases are not reproduced before a real C compatibility layer exists.

xpath-compatibility-tests.description: XPath and XPath Filter 2.0 use standards behavior by default; integration tests exercise the explicit libxmlsec1-compatible here() binding.

backend-provider-transform-surface.rationale: The native provider contract implements the corresponding cryptographic operation, but not this libxmlsec1 backend-specific C symbol.

binary-c-surface.rationale: The current deliverable is a native Rust crate and does not claim libxmlsec1 C source or binary compatibility.

deprecated-c-surface.rationale: Deprecated C aliases are excluded until the compatibility layer has a concrete ABI contract.

native-cli-behavior-options.rationale: The native CLI implements this provider-independent option with donor-compatible parsing and command behavior.

native-cli-commands.rationale: The native binary implements the libxmlsec1 command spelling and dispatch contract while capability checks delimit the available algorithm and key-data subsets.

native-cli-exit-status.rationale: Successful operations exit zero and parse, policy, capability, verification, cryptographic, and I/O failures exit non-zero.

native-cli-provider-options.rationale: The native CLI implements this option only for the formats, algorithms, or fixed RustCrypto provider behavior advertised by its capability registry.

native-sha1-verification-uri.rationale: The native Rust API implements SHA-1 reference digests; secure signing defaults reject SHA-1 while an explicit compatibility policy can opt in.

native-supported-uri.rationale: The native Rust API parses and executes this standard URI, with unit or interoperability coverage in the repository.

native-xpath-uri.rationale: The native Rust API implements XPath and XPath Filter 2.0 with standards-compliant here() semantics by default; reproducing libxmlsec1's divergent Transform-element binding requires the explicit XmlSecLegacy mode.

phaos-xmldsig-exhaustive.rationale: Every signature vector is executable and classified by the native public-pipeline suite; full family parity remains planned until its explicitly reported XSLT, HMAC-MD5, and MD5-signed certificate dependencies are implemented.

planned-cli-surface.rationale: This libxmlsec1 option or special status behavior is inventoried but is not yet reproduced by the native CLI.

planned-cli-verbose.rationale: The native CLI accepts this donor runner argument, but does not yet implement libxmlsec1's flag-controlled detailed error mode.

planned-donor-families.rationale: The upstream family is tracked as a parity target; individual covered vectors are recorded by native interoperability tests rather than claiming the whole family.

planned-key-format-surface.rationale: Native Rust key parsing exists, but the libxmlsec1 key-format enum contract is not yet reproduced.

planned-registry-surface.rationale: libxmlsec1 registry entry points are inventoried for the future compatibility layer and are not exposed by the native API.

policy-gated-legacy-uri.rationale: The implementation retains this legacy algorithm for interoperability, but the compiled policy must explicitly permit it.

remaining-backend-surface.rationale: This libxmlsec1 backend-specific C capability is not represented by the current native provider contract.

remaining-uri-surface.rationale: The URI is part of the libxmlsec1 1.3.13 public vocabulary but is not yet implemented by the native Rust API.
